brief: A small-parts organizer with at least six separate bins.

requirements.evidence: Half-depth bins (about 48 mm deep) suit small parts such as screws, nuts and standoffs. I put example props in them to show this.
There are 6 separate bins, one in each cell: bin:0,0,0, 1,0,0, 2,0,0, 0,1,0, 1,1,0 and -1,1,0.

finish.summary: I built a small-parts organizer from six hex cells joined together, with one half-depth bin (hex-bin-half) in each cell. That gives six separate bins. The outer faces are closed with solid end caps, and the joints between cells are bolted together. To show what it's for, I put M3 screws, nuts, standoffs, a solder reel and electrical tape in the bins. All the props can be seen from above. They sit below the bin rims, so they're harder to see from the side. The build check passed with no rule issues, and the collision check came back clear. The build has 30 parts, and the estimate is about 2,649 g of filament and 3,732 minutes (about 62 hours) of printing.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
